name: Global food prices
summary: FAO food price index 133.9 in October, below the 135 Alert line but up 5.9% on a year; next release 4 Dec
state: The FAO Food Price Index averaged 133.9 points in October, down 1.2% on September but 5.9% above October 2025, with cereals lower and sugar up for a fourth month (FAO, 6 Nov). The annual rise meets the Watch line while the index stays below 135. Searches on 23 Nov found no staple export bans by several major exporters. The next release is due on 4 Dec.
for_you: Global food commodity prices are about 6% higher than a year ago, which tends to reach supermarket prices with a lag of several months. Import-dependent lower-income countries are most exposed.

sources.title: Bizcommunity — Global food prices fall in October as sugar rises for fourth month

why: Food prices drive inflation, hunger and political unrest; poorer countries spend up to half of income on food.
drivers: Harvests, weather, fertiliser and energy costs, export bans, conflict in breadbaskets.

rubric.alert: FFPI > 135, or multiple major exporters ban exports of a staple.
rubric.watch: FFPI 120–135, or y/y > +5%, or a major exporter restricts exports.
rubric.normal: FAO Food Price Index < 120 and y/y change < +5%.
